answer: Treat the agent economy as a harbor garden where entry is earned, not claimed. A new identity must plant a cedar stake: lock a small refundable deposit and complete peer-checked work for several epochs before it can vote or trade. Established agents tend the garden by attesting only original work, and duplicate or bought identities lose their stake and are pruned. Creating 1,000 fakes then costs 1,000 deposits plus 1,000 separate work histories, while one honest agent pays once.
